intent: One data cell of a table row.
typical_uses: One value of a record in a TableBody row
A totals value in a TableFooter row

dont_use_when.situation: The heading of a column or of a row

invariants.text: With `pinned` the cell is position sticky and stacks above the cells scrolling under it (one step above the header cells under `stickyHeader` or `variant="collection"`), so a column stays in view while a table wider than its wrapper scrolls sideways. Table declares no offset: a column pins at the sum of the widths pinned before it, which only the caller knows, so the caller gives `insetInlineStart` or `insetInlineEnd` in `style`. The cell is filled with the row's own fill over an opaque base, so it follows hover, `data-state` and any other state of its row; the base is `--table-pinned-fill`, read with `--card` as its fallback.
Cell text does not wrap: a long value widens its column and the table's wrapper scrolls horizontally. Under Table's `variant="collection"` cell text wraps instead.
TableCell is box-sizing border-box, so a width set through style or className includes the cell's padding; a cell holding a role="checkbox" descendant drops its inline-end padding.

anti_patterns.do_instead: Give the offset the column pins at; without one the cell sticks to no edge and scrolls away

anti_patterns.dont: Set display flex or grid on a TableCell to lay out its content
anti_patterns.do_instead: Wrap the content in an inner element and lay that out; a non-table display makes the cell stop being a table-cell box, so vertical-align no longer applies and the 40px floor becomes a fixed height

a11y.by: table.test.tsx asserts getAllByRole('cell') finds all four data cells of the rendered table

good.title: A first column that stays in view

bad.title: A flex layout on the cell itself
bad.why: The cell stops being a table-cell box and loses its vertical centering; put the flex layout on an element inside the cell.

bad.title: A pinned cell with no offset
bad.why: Sticky needs an edge to stick to; with no `insetInlineStart` or `insetInlineEnd` the cell scrolls away with its row.
